title: Normalized affine Leray section equivalence before scalar extension
statement:
Let $f:X\to S$ be a quasi-compact quasi-separated morphism of schemes, and $F$ a quasi-coherent module on $X$ [def-pc-module-pullback]. Fix an injective resolution $I$ of $F$, a degree $p\in\mathbb N$, and an affine open $V\subset S$. Put $U=f^{-1}V$, $A=\Gamma(S,V)$, $h:U\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ the restricted morphism followed by the canonical affine chart, $N=F|_U$ computed by open-immersion pullback, and $P=R^pf_*F$. Let $R$ be any augmentation-preserving restricted resolution data for $I$ on $U$ [def-weil-pbc-flat-base-change-open-choices]. Let $E_M:H^p_{\mathrm{Mod}}(U,M)\simeq H^p(U,M)$ be a family of additive equivalences natural for all module morphisms, with module right-derived sections [pqf-def-cohomology] and the Ext cohomology model [def-pc-flat-cohomology-comparison]. Define $e_H$ by applying $E$ to the restriction of $F$ and transporting through the canonical restriction/pullback isomorphism. There is an $A$-linear equivalence $e:HOver(h,N,p)\simeq_A\Gamma(P,V)$ whose value on $\xi$ equals the class map resolutionSectionClass for $R$, followed by the inverse resolution comparison for $f_*$, applied to $e_H^{-1}(\xi)$. There is no base-change scheme, ring extension, second resolution or flatness hypothesis.

proof.text: Let c be the specified additive resolution class map. The affine resolution section bijectivity theorem proves that c is bijective independently of any Ext comparison E.

For a in Gamma(S,V), let b be its image via GammaSpecIso inverse and h.appTop, and let e be H.mapLinearEquiv of restrictFunctorIsoPullback. Apply hE to multiplication by b on the restricted module, then apply e and its map_smul identity. This proves eH(C(mu_b)(x))=a*eH(x). Injectivity of eH gives eH inverse(a*xi)=C(mu_b)(eH inverse(xi)). The scalar class-map theorem therefore proves that c composed with eH inverse is linear. Additivity follows from the two additive maps.

The function c composed with eH inverse is bijective by Function.Bijective.comp. Apply LinearEquiv.ofBijective to the linear map just constructed. Its forward function is definitionally the required expression, so the normalization equality follows by reflexivity for every xi.
